summary: This program tracks a coffee order's progress from 0% to 100%, printing the status at each step and announcing when the drink is ready. It uses a while loop, which keeps repeating as long as its condition stays true.

lines.text: The counter starts at zero because the order has made no progress yet. A while loop needs this variable to exist before the loop begins, since the loop's condition tests it.
Java checks this condition before each pass through the loop body. Using <= rather than < means 100 itself gets printed, so the reader sees the full range from 0% to 100%.
Joining text and a number with + turns the number into text, producing a line like "Coffee order status: 30%".
This is the step that eventually ends the loop. Forgetting to change the variable a while condition depends on is the classic cause of an infinite loop.
Sitting outside the loop's braces, this runs once after the condition finally fails and the loop is done.
